neighbours.label: a quantity defined in words by other quantities (textbook formula or word problem): the function word leading into the next quantity ('equals its mass times ⟦its⟧', 'equal to ⟦the⟧ cost price ⟦of⟧', 'rate of change ⟦of⟧')
fire: The kinetic energy of a car equals half its mass times the square of its speed.
Pressure is defined as the force divided by the area of the surface.
A shopkeeper sells 15 chairs and earns a profit equal to the cost price of 3 chairs.
The weight of an object equals its mass times the acceleration of gravity.
Density is the mass of a substance divided by its volume.
A farmer sells 40 sheep and makes a loss equal to the selling price of 5 sheep.
The work done on a box equals the force times the distance of the push.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
quiet: The old car in the garage belongs to a friend of my father.
Pressure from the board forced the director to leave the company.
A shopkeeper sells chairs and lamps in a narrow street behind the church.
The weight of the decision kept her awake for most of the night.
Density of traffic is a common complaint among people in the city.
A farmer sells his sheep every autumn and spends the winter in town.
The work on the box office hit took the crew almost two years.
Acceleration of the reforms was a promise of the new government.
